etymology: Latin: "to the point of sickness" - the argument that wins by making the audience tired.
committed_when: A claim has been answered once and the answer was not accepted.
tell: The same sentence returns unchanged, and the replies get shorter.
counter: Answer once, note that the answer stands, and stop. Repetition is a contest of stamina, and it can be declined.
senses: Repeating a claim until objection feels pointless, and treating the exhaustion as agreement.
It works on volume rather than content. Nobody can answer the same sentence forty times, so the fortieth repetition lands unanswered and looks unanswerable.
example: *"It was the biggest crowd ever. Biggest crowd. Everyone agrees it was the biggest crowd."* Three sentences, one claim, no count.

confused_with.tell: Proof by assertion repeats to sound certain; ad nauseam repeats to make the audience stop asking.
